He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|2|in|sp=us|abbr=off}} and {{convert|185|lb|abbr=off}}, he plays the [[point guard]] position. The son of [[Greg Anthony]], who played 11 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), he grew up in [[Manhattan]], New York and attended [[Archbishop Molloy High School]] before transferring to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] for his final year. He was rated a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the best point guard in the 2019 class. As a senior, he earned [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA first team]] honors and was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) of the [[McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]], and [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. In his freshman season at North Carolina, Anthony earned third-team All-ACC accolades despite missing six weeks due to injury. In 2018, Anthony led the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] to a gold medal and was named to the all-tournament team at the [[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship|FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]] in [[St. Catharines|St. Catharines, Ontario]]. ==Early life== Anthony was born in [[Portland, Oregon]], where his father, [[Greg Anthony]], was playing for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. His [[umbilical cord]] was [[nuchal cord|wrapped around his neck]] at birth, affecting his heart rate at the time but not leading to further complications.{{cite web |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |title=Ex-NBA player Greg Anthony's heralded son, Cole, to make waves in college basketball |url=https://andscape.com/features/ex-nba-player-greg-anthonys-heralded-son-cole-to-make-college-choice/ |website=[[Andscape]] |access-date=July 17, 2019 |date=April 22, 2019}} As a toddler, Anthony's family moved to [[Manhattan]], where he grew up in a [[Penthouse apartment|penthouse]].{{cite web |last=O'Donnell |first=Ricky |title=Cole Anthony is built for greatness |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2019/4/19/18485587/cole-anthony-recruiting-north-carolina-oregon-nba-draft-highlights |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=November 7, 2019 |date=April 19, 2019}} Even though he came from a wealthy family, Anthony's parents insisted on raising him with hard-working values. He later commented, "They don't hand anything to me in life. What they do hand to me is knowledge."{{cite web |last=Dauster |first=Rob |title=Rising Son: Cole Anthony remains grounded as he follows his father's footsteps |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/07/25/rising-son-cole-anthony-remains-grounded-as-he-follows-his-fathers-footsteps/ |publisher=[[NBC Sports]] |access-date=November 6, 2019 |date=November 6, 2019}} Anthony first played [[baseball]], a sport his father initially thought he would pursue,{{cite web |last=Hale |first=David M. |title=Wired like Kobe and MJ: Cole Anthony is the freshman you need to know |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/27968152 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=November 7, 2019 |date=November 6, 2019}} but decided to focus on basketball in fifth grade. In his childhood, he worked with private basketball trainers and played [[pick-up game]]s at local parks, seeking out older opponents.{{cite web |last=Pina |first=Michael |title=Cole Anthony Wants to Revolutionize Basketball (And Play Zelda) |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/cole-anthony-wants-to-revolutionize-basketball-and-play-zelda-the-16-project/ |website=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]] |access-date=November 6, 2018 |date=October 23, 2017}} From a young age, Anthony was coached by Steve Harris, who mentored NBA player [[Kemba Walker]] and was a prominent [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) figure in New York. When he was 11 years old, he appeared in ''Little Ballers'', a 2013 [[Nickelodeon]] [[documentary film]] directed by his mother, [[Crystal McCrary]]. The film featured Anthony's New York-based AAU team, New Heights.{{cite web |last=Parks |first=Chanel |title='Little Ballers' Documentary Teaches Us That Black Boys Aren't Monolithic |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/little-ballers-documentary_n_6742920 |website=[[HuffPost]] |access-date=November 7, 2019 |date=December 6, 2017}} ==High school career== In his first three years of high school, Anthony played basketball for [[Archbishop Molloy High School]] in [[Briarwood, Queens|Briarwood, New York]]. He was the first freshman to immediately start at point guard for Molloy. [[Christ the King Regional High School]] head coach Joe Arbitello called Anthony "the best point guard I've seen since [[Stephon Marbury]] at that age."{{cite web |last=Braziller |first=Zach |title='Best since Marbury': Young face of NY HS hoops is Greg Anthony's son |url=https://nypost.com/2016/01/23/best-since-marbury-young-face-of-ny-hs-hoops-is-greg-anthonys-son/ |website=[[New York Post]] |access-date=July 23, 2019 |date=January 23, 2016}} Anthony averaged 16.9 points and 6.7 rebounds per game and garnered All-[[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] (CHSAA) Class AA second team recognition.{{cite web |last=Mancari |first=Jim |title=The Tablet's All-Star Boys' HS Hoops Team |url=https://thetablet.org/the-tablets-all-star-boys-hs-hoops-team/ |website=[[The Tablet (Brooklyn)|The Tablet]] |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=March 30, 2016}} As a sophomore, Anthony led Molloy to the CHSAA Class AA city championship finals, where his team was upset by [[Cardinal Hayes High School]].{{cite web |last=Libert |first=Mike |title=Hayes Shocks Molloy; Wins CHSAA "AA" Championship |url=https://nychoops.rivals.com/news/hayes-shocks-molloy-wins-chsaa-aa-championship |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=March 12, 2017}} He recorded a season-high 31 points in a win over [[Iona Preparatory School|Iona Prep]] in December 2016.{{cite web He was named All-CHSAA Class AA first team, [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA third team]], and [[MaxPreps]] Junior All-American third team.{{cite web |last=Mancari |first=Jim |title=Boys' High School Basketball All Stars |url=https://thetablet.org/boys-high-school-basketball-all-stars/ |website=[[The Tablet (Brooklyn)|The Tablet]] |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=March 22, 2018}}{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=2017-18 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/hNi1UD2amUag_PSRxexoDw/2017-18-maxpreps-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team-.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=April 13, 2018}}{{cite web |title=ALL-USA Boys Basketball: Third Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-boys-basketball-third-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=April 4, 2018}} He scored a season-best 37 points against John Marshall High School at the City of Palms Classic in December 2017.{{cite web |last=Snow |first=Brian |title=Top Performers: City of Palms Day 4 |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Trendon-Watford-and-Cole-Anthony-made-a-statement-at-City-of-Palms-112617533/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=December 21, 2017}} In July 2018, Anthony won the [[most valuable player]] (MVP) award with the PSA Cardinals in the Nike EYBL after averaging 26.9 points, 7.6 rebounds, and 3.5 assists over 16 games.{{cite web |last=Kinsky |first=Alec |title=NIKE EYBL Most Valuable Player: Cole Anthony |url=https://www.d1circuit.com/news_article/show/932395 |publisher=D1 Circuit |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=July 6, 2018}} On July 28, 2018, Anthony announced that he would transfer to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] for his senior year.
